purpose:
A single-user macOS dictation application. It captures speech, recognizes it, optionally rewrites it under a user-selected mode, and inserts the result into the application the user was working in. Every speech and language operation runs on the user's Mac. There is no cloud fallback, no account, no subscription gate, and no artificial cap on recording length or usage; the limits are the hardware and the models the user installs.

In scope: recording controls, text delivery, recording display, built-in modes, custom modes, automatic mode selection, vocabulary, context, languages, input sources, meetings, history, models, desktop behavior. Out of scope: cloud inference, account-based settings synchronization, paywalls, enterprise billing and authentication, and any Windows or iOS client.

The whole product is designed before implementation work is cut, because several requirements constrain the persistence schema, the process model and the ingest boundary in ways that are expensive to retrofit: re-recognizing old audio through a different speech model while keeping every derived artifact attributable (D-029), generating meeting notes from a transcript plus a diarization result plus an editable speaker assignment (D-037), deleting a recording while a worker is producing a result for it (D-024, D-033), snapshotting mode settings so a later edit cannot change the meaning of a saved result (D-006), recovering a crash at any stage without duplicating delivered text (D-010, D-031), and bounding memory on a multi-hour import across a process boundary (D-018). Left to whichever implementation task first encounters them, those force the schema and the job model into a shape that cannot express them.

This revision settles the items the last review found unresolved. Diarization and note generation are stages of the run machine with their own cancellation, recovery and provenance rows, and notes pin every input they used (D-037, D-006, D-007, D-031). Delivery confirmation is a predicate over the expected text at the expected location rather than a length comparison, with a complete attempt-state table and one named target per focus outcome (D-008, D-009, D-010). The capture journal states its write, fsync, index and delete order and carries the per-packet metadata that reconstruction needs (D-030). Diarization runs in a named sandboxed service and enters residency and admission accounting (D-003, D-004, D-027). Model installations gain an archived state, so replacing a runtime releases weights while History stays attributable (D-038). Distribution is a decision rather than a blocking question (D-036). Media resume runs only through a player integration that identifies the player and observes the pause transition (D-025). Preview degradation keeps provisional text rather than dropping it (D-011).

Where a claim cannot be made, the design says so instead of weakening the feature. Lexical and structural checks on generated text are necessary conditions, not proof of fidelity, so D-012 states which checks run, what happens when a check is unavailable, and what the runtime does with text whose compliance cannot be established. Speaker attribution keeps absent evidence as unknown and keeps manual assignment available (D-023). Every measurement that would evaluate a runtime choice is named, given an acceptance range and an action on failure, and marked unperformed (D-034).

The historical feature inventories from the mcwhisper and super experiments are evidence about desired scope. Their generated plans and dependency choices do not bind this design.
architecture:
## Layering rule

One rule governs dependency direction. DictationCore depends only on DictationPorts; adapters depend on DictationPorts and on system frameworks; nothing depends on an adapter except the composition root in the app shell. DictationCore contains no AppKit, no AVFoundation, no SQLite and no XPC code, so the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, output checking and scheduling policy can be exercised without a microphone, a model or a window server.

## Package and target layout (D-002)

A Swift Package Manager package, LocalDictation, with library targets:

- DictationPorts: protocols and value types shared by core and adapters (AudioSource, AudioFrame, SpeechRecognizer, TextGenerator, Diarizer, DecoderProvider, TextInserter, FocusObserver, ContextProvider, ModelStore, RecordingStore, LeaseBroker, ShortcutRegistrar, MediaPlayerAdapter, RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor).
- DictationCore: run state machine, RunManifest assembly, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, ResourceScheduler policy, delivery policy.
- TextValidation: transformation contracts, the language-independent check set, per-language validator packs covering segmentation, interrogative detection and content-word extraction.
- DictationStore: SQLite schema, migrations, repositories, the audio chunk journal and its sealer, tombstones, generations, the lease broker.
- AudioIngest: AVAudioEngine microphone source, ScreenCaptureKit system-audio source, AVAssetReader seekable file source, converters to the canonical recognition format.
- SpeechRuntimeWhisperKit, with SpeechRuntimeWhisperCpp built when Intel coverage is required (D-020); DiarizerSpeakerKit (D-023); LanguageRuntimeLlamaCpp (D-021). Each publishes a RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor.
- InferenceIPC: message types and the connection client shared by the app and the services.
- SystemIntegration: accessibility insertion, pasteboard, CGEventTap shortcuts, player adapters, status item, permission probes.
- DictationUI: SwiftUI views, recording panel, settings, history browser.

Five bundled XPC services. Four carry code that must not reach the network: SpeechService, GenerationService, DiarizationService and DecodeService. The fifth, ModelDownloader, is the only one that may. Each service is a thin main over a library target, so swift test covers its logic. The Xcode app target produces the bundles and owns entitlements, hardened runtime, privacy usage strings and notarization, none of which is expressible in Package.swift.

## Process model (D-003, D-028, D-036)

The app shell runs unsandboxed, because setting selected text in other applications and running a session-level event tap are unavailable to a sandboxed application outside the Mac App Store; D-036 records the distribution decision that makes this available. Each inference service is sandboxed on its own and its entitlement set omits com.apple.security.network.client, so an outbound connection is denied by the system whatever the linked code contains. Model files reach a service as opened file descriptors, or through a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs for a runtime that insists on opening a model directory by path; which of the two applies is the output of gate F2. Audio crosses the connection in bounded windows under the credit protocol of D-018.

Diarization has its own service rather than sharing SpeechService, for two reasons stated in D-023: RESEARCH records that this runtime's default initialization may download models, so it is the component whose acquisition control most needs an enforced boundary, and it loads a different model set whose residency must be accounted separately from the speech model's single-slot rule (D-027).

Nothing listens on a TCP port. A local HTTP endpoint would bind a port every process on the machine can reach, would need its own authentication, and is the component most likely to acquire forwarding behavior through configuration the app does not own; RESEARCH raises that for llama.cpp's server tooling.

ModelDownloader holds the network entitlement, an allowlist of model hosts, and write access confined to Models/.staging. It runs only on explicit user action, and no inference service can start it.

A service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, so connection interruption is a first-class event. The run fails at its current stage, committed results stand, and the next admission loads the model into a fresh service. A service holds only state the app can rebuild from the run manifest and the store: its loaded models, the current job's window queue, and that job's decoder state.

## Processing runs (D-029, D-037)

A recording owns audio artifacts. Every piece of derived text belongs to a processing_run, which pins the settings that produced it and names its entry stage. Run kinds: dictation, covering capture through delivery; import; meeting, covering two-stream capture through notes; reprocess_recognition; reprocess_diarization; reprocess_text; reprocess_notes. Only dictation runs may deliver text.

## Run stages

The stage set is idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting, delivering, terminal. A run enters at the stage its kind declares and visits only the stages its kind declares; every stage a run can occupy has a cancellation effect (D-007) and a recovery transition (D-031).

## The lifetime of a dictation run (D-006)

Component boundaries follow this sequence.

1. idle.
2. arming. The microphone stream starts immediately on the trigger and its frames go into a pre-roll ring, so the first word is not lost while the rest of arming runs concurrently: resolve the effective mode from the automatic-selection rules (D-014); latch the delivery target, meaning frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element and the readback capability of that element (D-008); sample context sources in parallel against a 200 ms budget (D-016); assemble a RunManifest naming mode revision, speech model installation, language model installation, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag and validator pack set; allocate a UUIDv7 recording id and run id; create the session directory; write and fsync manifest v0 with disposition=active.
3. capturing. The pre-roll ring is flushed into the chunk journal ahead of the live frames (D-030); the writer appends timestamped native frames; the provisional recognizer consumes a parallel tap; the panel shows live text and an envelope (D-011).
4. sealing. Stop the source, finish encoding the journal into the library artifact, fsync, then commit the recording row, artifact row and run row in one transaction. That is the first point at which the recording exists in History; ownership before that point is the session directory itself (D-033).
5. recognizing. One pass over the complete audio produces a recognition result with segment timings and per-segment average log-probability. The provisional stream is discarded instead of promoted; it was computed over partial context and is a different artifact.
6. refining. Deterministic vocabulary replacement and optional filler removal produce a normalized result derived from that recognition result (D-015).
7. rewriting, only when the mode has a generation stage: prompt assembly, generation in the service, contract checking (D-012).
8. delivering. Exactly one ladder attempt sequence, guarded by a committed idempotency record (D-010).
9. terminal: complete, cancelled(stage), failed(stage, reason), or delivery_unresolved.

Imports enter at capturing with a seekable source and no delivery latch. Meetings enter at arming with two sources, no delivery latch, and continue capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, noting. Reprocessing enters at recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting or noting with a manifest that names its parent inputs. One machine serves every input source and every reprocessing path, which is why cancellation, recovery and deletion each have a single definition.

## Concurrency and ownership (D-004)

One RunActor per processing run owns that run's state, rows and files, and is the only writer for them. Two runs on the same recording are serialized by the recording's lease (D-033). The audio callback thread never touches an actor, allocates or locks; it writes frames and a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope into two lock-free rings.

A single ResourceScheduler actor admits model-bound work. Capture is not model-bound and is not admitted: the capture writer and the incremental sealer run on a dedicated capture lane with a quality-of-service above batch work and no admission gate, so a long import cannot starve the sealer that keeps the journal window bounded. The interactive lane covers the provisional pass and the recognition and rewrite for the run the user is waiting on. The batch lane covers imports, diarization, meeting notes and reprocessing. Model slots are counted separately per model kind: at most one speech model, one generation model and one diarization model set resident, and admission additionally checks the summed footprint against the budget in D-027, so a diarization job runs beside recognition only when both fit.

Whether an admitted batch job can be preempted is read from the runtime's measured capability descriptor, which records cancellation latency, whether a window boundary is a safe checkpoint, and whether resuming from a checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript. A runtime whose descriptor records verified checkpoint equivalence yields at the next window and resumes. Any runtime without that verified field is cancelled and restarted from the beginning of the job, or allowed to finish behind a bound the panel displays. Restarting from a checkpoint is used only where the descriptor establishes the checkpoint is equivalent; whole-job restart is the default because it is correct without that evidence.

## Component responsibilities

- ModeResolver (core): a pure function from foreground application, URL when readable, explicit override and the ordered rule list to a mode revision.
- VocabularyPipeline (core): pure text-to-text with an explicit stage order and ICU-based segmentation.
- PromptAssembler (core): mode instructions, then context in the form D-016 allows for its source, fenced with a per-run random delimiter and labeled as reference material, then the normalized transcript, then the task line restated.
- ContractChecker (TextValidation): runs the language-independent check set always and the language-dependent set when a pack exists, and reports which checks ran; disposition of a failed or unavailable check is decided in core by D-012.
- DeliveryCoordinator (core policy) with TextInserter (adapter): focus policy, target selection and the confirmation predicate separated from insertion mechanism, so policy is testable without a window server.
- RecordingStore with LeaseBroker (DictationStore): the only writers of History rows and library files, and the enforcement point for tombstones, generations and leases for every writer including retention.
- InferenceClient (InferenceIPC): connection lifecycle, credit accounting, interruption handling, per-service residency accounting.

## Why this supports the whole scope as capabilities land

The run state machine, the manifest snapshot, the provenance graph, the recovery table and the lease protocol are built first against fake adapters. Every later capability adds an adapter behind an existing port, a result kind, or a validator language pack. None of them changes how a run is recorded, cancelled, recovered or deleted. The parts that are expensive to change late are exercised against fakes, where cancel-at-every-stage and kill-at-every-boundary suites are cheap to run.

## Stores and ownership

DictationStore owns everything under ~/Library/Application Support/LocalDictation/:

```
library.sqlite                                  metadata, runs, results, FTS index (WAL)
Recordings/<uuid>/manifest.json                 fsynced at run start, carries disposition
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/<seq>.pcm    durable capture chunks
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/index.log    packet index for sealing
Recordings/<uuid>/audio/<stream>.caf            sealed library artifact
Recordings/<uuid>/source/<original filename>    imported original
Models/blobs/<sha256>/                          immutable verified installs
Models/.staging/<uuid>/                         in-flight downloads and imports
Scratch/<jobId>/                                service temporaries
```

One writer connection in WAL mode; readers use separate connections. RunActor never writes SQLite directly. It calls repository methods that enforce tombstone, generation and lease rules.

## Ownership before the History row exists (D-033)

A lease requires a recording row, and capture creates that row only at the sealing commit. Between arming and that commit the unit of ownership is the session directory: its path contains a UUIDv7 no other actor can name, the owning RunActor is its only writer, and manifest.json carries a disposition field, fsynced on change, with values active, cancelled and abandoned. Cancellation or deletion requested before the commit is recorded by writing the disposition, not by a tombstone row. Recovery treats a session directory with no committed recording row according to its manifest disposition, which is what makes pre-commit cancellation durable across a crash. The lease protocol begins at the commit and covers everything afterwards.

## Provenance graph (D-029, D-037)

- recordings(id, created_at, source_kind, duration_ms, interrupted, deleted_at, generation, audio_state, display_run_id)
- audio_artifacts(id, recording_id, role, path, container, codec, sample_rate, channels, sealed_at, sha256, byte_length), role in {microphone, system, imported_original}
- processing_runs(id, recording_id, recording_generation, kind, entry_stage, manifest_json, state, started_at, ended_at, reason)
- results(id, run_id, recording_id, kind, primary_input_result_id, text, params_json, params_rendered, created_at), kind in {recognition, normalized, rewritten, translation, diarization, notes}
- result_inputs(result_id, input_result_id, role), role in {transcript, diarization, prior_notes}
- segments, speaker_clusters, speaker_identities, speaker_identity_names, speaker_assignment_revisions, speaker_assignments, modes, mode_revisions, vocabulary_revisions, rules, model_installations, model_assets, active_models, leases, context_digests, delivery_attempts, delivery_profiles, jobs

Every result names its primary input. A recognition result has primary_input_result_id NULL and roots its run's chain; normalized derives from recognition; rewritten derives from normalized; a translation derives from whichever result the user translated; a diarization result derives from nothing textual and names its audio artifacts in its params. A notes result has the transcript as its primary input and additional result_inputs rows for the diarization result it used, so a result with several inputs is representable rather than flattened into one foreign key. A recording can hold several recognition results and several diarization results, one per run, each carrying the model installation that produced it. Results are immutable after insert, enforced by a trigger that rejects UPDATE on results.text; reprocessing inserts and never replaces. recordings.display_run_id is a user-movable pointer deciding what the list view shows.

## Speaker assignments as revisions (D-037)

A diarization result is immutable and holds cluster boundaries. The mapping from segment to named speaker is separate and versioned: speaker_assignment_revisions(id, recording_id, diarization_result_id, content_hash, created_at) with speaker_assignments(revision_id, segment_id, identity_id, attribution_state). Every user edit, whether an assignment, a merge or a split, appends a revision. Identity display names are themselves append-only in speaker_identity_names(identity_id, name, effective_from), because a rename must not silently change what an older transcript view showed.

A notes run pins the diarization result id, the assignment revision id and the identity-name set hash in its manifest and in result_inputs. Note text is immutable and contains the names in effect at generation, so a later rename or a re-run of diarization cannot change the note's meaning. History compares the pinned identifiers against current state and shows, on a note, that speakers were renamed or re-diarized since it was produced, with a regenerate action.

## Persistence choice (D-005)

SQLite through GRDB with FTS5 over result text. History search is a stated requirement and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is why SQLite wins here; SwiftData and Core Data have no comparable text index and their migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures. Schema versions are numbered migrations, each with a test that runs the migration against a fixture database captured at the prior version.

## Audio: journal, sealing and artifacts (D-030)

Capture writes fixed-period chunks, two seconds by default, of raw interleaved Int16 at the source's native rate into journal/<stream>/. Each chunk is written to <seq>.pcm.part, fsynced, renamed to <seq>.pcm, and the directory is fsynced. A chunk carries no header; its format lives in the fsynced manifest, so any complete chunk decodes on its own and a torn final chunk is discardable.

The incremental sealer runs on the capture lane. Its cycle for chunk N is ordered so that the index never names bytes that are not durable:

1. Encode chunk N into ALAC packets.
2. Append the packet bytes to the CAF data chunk in audio/<stream>.caf. The data chunk's size field is written as -1 during capture, which CAF defines as extending to end of file, so no header rewrite is needed while recording.
3. fsync the CAF file. Audio bytes are durable before anything refers to them.
4. Append one record to index.log and fsync it. The record is {magic, record_seq, chunk_seq, first_packet_index, packet_count, frames_per_packet, caf_data_byte_offset, caf_data_byte_length, varint packet byte sizes for each of packet_count packets, crc32 over the whole record}. The per-packet sizes are present because an ALAC packet table cannot be reconstructed from a count and an offset alone.
5. Delete the journal chunks whose packets are covered by durable index records, then fsync the journal directory.

This keeps transient journal storage near a 30-second window instead of the whole recording. At the end of capture the sealer writes the CAF pakt chunk from index.log, patches the data chunk size, fsyncs, records the artifact sha256, and the run commits.

The design does not assume a truncated container can be finalized. After a crash, recovery replays index.log from the start, accepting records whose crc32 validates and whose byte range lies within the file's actual length; the first record failing either test ends the durable prefix and the rest of the log is discarded, which is how a torn tail is rejected. The CAF data chunk is truncated to the end of the last accepted record, the pakt chunk is built from the accepted records, and surviving journal chunks after that point are re-encoded and appended. Worst-case loss is the unsealed tail: at most one chunk period plus data the operating system had not yet flushed within it. The exact bound comes from gate F3, which has not been run; the chunk period is the tuning knob if the measurement is worse than expected, and the structural fallback if reconstruction proves invalid at any period is to stop deleting chunks until the finalized artifact has been decoded end to end and hashed, at the cost of journal storage equal to the whole recording.

Canonical recognition format is 16 kHz mono Float32, produced by a converter stage after the ingest port instead of at the source. Sealed dictation audio is 16 kHz mono ALAC at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour, by arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour; meeting streams are sealed at native rate, which is larger and is reported in the library size view. Lossy encoding is rejected because re-recognition with a better model later is a requirement. Imported files are copied in their original encoding and decoded on demand.

## Model installations, their states and their notices (D-022, D-038)

model_installations records identity (publisher, revision string, sha256 over the ordered weight file set), runtime kind, model kind, declared capabilities, install time, origin and lifecycle state in {installed, archived, missing}. model_assets records one row per weight file with its own sha256, size, license identifier and the path of the retained notice text. RESEARCH observes that a development kit's license does not describe every model a user might import, and that the public diarization collection carries component-specific notices; recording the notice per asset is what lets the model manager state terms for the exact weights installed. The application bundles no weights.

Archiving is what bounds storage when a runtime is replaced (D-038): the installation row, hashes, capabilities and notices are retained so every History result stays attributable, while the weight blobs are released. Results also carry params_rendered, a human-readable snapshot of the parameters written at insert time, so an old row remains readable after its adapter is removed from the build.

## Settings snapshots and derived results

A mode is a named entity with an append-only chain of mode_revisions, each content-addressed over prompt, formatting rules, transformation contract, validator language list and model selections. A run's manifest stores revision identifiers. Editing a mode creates a revision and leaves saved results pointing at the revision that produced them, which makes the requirement that later edits must not silently change a saved result structural instead of procedural. History shows the producing revision and diffs it against the current one.

## Context retention and ephemeral lifetimes (D-016)

By default the store keeps a SHA-256 digest, byte length and source kind per context sample in context_digests, and not the text. That is enough to tell a user reprocessing an old recording that the original context is unavailable, without retaining copies of unrelated documents and screens. Retaining the text is opt-in per mode, shown in History, and deleted with the recording.

The transient copies have stated lifetimes. A captured screen frame lives only inside the arming task, is passed to Vision in memory and is released when text extraction returns; it is never written to disk. Clipboard text and accessibility text live in the RunActor until the prompt is assembled, then are dropped unless retention is opted in. XPC message buffers are released as credit is returned per window. Generation key-value state is freed at job end or at model unload. Scratch/<jobId> is removed when the job ends and swept at launch. No inference service writes prompts, context or transcripts to disk; DecodeService writes decoded audio windows into its job scratch and nothing else.

## Interrupted operations (D-031)

The ordering rule is stated once: an externally visible irreversible effect is preceded by a durable record of intent, which is what delivery does, while a local idempotent effect is followed by its commit, which is what sealing does. Recovery at launch reconciles manifests, files and rows by run state.

- arming: remove the session directory. No rows.
- capturing: seal the journal, commit the recording with interrupted set, mark the run cancelled(capturing, crash). Nothing was delivered; History offers recognition.
- sealing: a sealed artifact may exist without rows. Re-sealing is idempotent because it derives from the journal and index.log, so recovery completes it and commits as above. If the manifest disposition is cancelled, recovery applies the cancellation disposition instead of committing.
- recognizing: no partial transcript is saved; the run becomes failed(recognizing, interrupted); audio is retained; History offers a new recognition run.
- diarizing: no partial diarization is saved; the run becomes failed(diarizing, interrupted); the recognition result and audio stand; History offers a new diarization run.
- refining: the recognition result is committed and immutable, and refining is a pure function of committed inputs pinned in the manifest, so recovery re-runs it, commits the normalized result and stops.
- rewriting: the run becomes failed(rewriting, interrupted); the normalized result stands; History offers a rewrite run. Recovery never resumes generation.
- noting: the run becomes failed(noting, interrupted); the transcript, diarization result and assignment revision stand; History offers a new notes run. Recovery never resumes generation.
- delivering: any delivery_attempts row in a non-terminal state or in unconfirmed becomes needs_review, the run becomes delivery_unresolved, and nothing is re-posted (D-010).
- Scratch directories, staged model directories and model blobs with no referencing installed row and no live lease are removed. Leases with no live holder are reclaimed.

## Deletion during active processing (D-024, D-033)

Deletion sets recordings.deleted_at, increments recordings.generation, and signals cancellation to every lease holder. Each worker carries recording id and generation from admission. A worker's commit is one transaction that re-reads the recording row and aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation; on abort it removes its scratch directory and returns. The existence check and the insert cannot be separated, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording, and the generation counter covers delete-then-recreate at the same identifier. Deleting a recording that has not yet committed is the pre-commit disposition path above.

Hard deletion of rows, artifacts and FTS entries runs when the last lease on the recording is released, and again at launch. Until then the recording is hidden and reported as deleting instead of as reclaimed space.

## Retention (D-033)

Retention defaults to keeping everything. Optional age-based, size-based and audio-discarding policies are ordinary deletion jobs: they acquire the same leases, observe the same generation checks, and skip any recording with a live lease held by a worker, a player or an export, retrying on the next pass. Discarding audio moves recordings.audio_state to audio_discarded, which History displays; playback, re-recognition and re-diarization are then unavailable while text reprocessing remains available. The first run of any policy lists exactly what it would remove before removing it.

## Cancellation by run stage (D-007)

Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage a run can occupy, and the panel names that effect when it happens. Cancelling one run never alters results committed by another run.

- arming: nothing kept; the pre-roll ring and session directory are discarded; no rows.
- capturing: capture stops; the journal is discarded by default and no History row is created; a per-mode setting seals it as an interrupted recording instead.
- sealing: the seal runs to completion, because it is bounded, idempotent and needed for any disposition to be coherent. The run then applies the capture-stage disposition: by default the sealed artifact and session directory are removed and no row is committed; under the per-mode setting the recording commits marked interrupted. No later stage is entered.
- recognizing: the worker stops at its next checkpoint; audio is kept; the run is marked cancelled; no partial transcript is saved, because a truncated transcript that looks complete is worse than none.
- diarizing: the worker stops; the recognition result and audio are kept; no partial diarization is saved, because a segment set covering part of a meeting would be indistinguishable in the transcript view from one covering all of it.
- refining: the recognition result stands; the normalized result is dropped.
- rewriting: generation stops; the normalized result is kept and offered for delivery.
- noting: generation stops; the transcript, diarization result and assignment revision stand; no partial notes are saved.
- delivering: cancellable until the first event is posted or the first accessibility write is issued. After that the app reports that delivery was attempted, records the attempt state, and stops; it does not try to undo an edit in another application.

## Permissions as a capability matrix (D-032)

Revocation is handled per capability and per run state in place of one global rule. Losing a capability terminates only the work that capability serves.

- Microphone denied at launch: recording controls disabled with a link to the settings pane; file import still works. Revoked during capturing: capture stops, the journal is sealed, the recording is marked interrupted, nothing is delivered.
- Screen Recording denied: system audio and screen context unavailable; microphone recording, all modes, and rules that do not need screen context continue; meetings degrade to microphone only with a visible marker. Revoked during capturing of a meeting: the system stream ends and is marked truncated at a timestamp, the microphone stream continues, and the recording states which streams cover which interval.
- Accessibility denied or revoked: selected-text insertion and readback are unavailable, so delivery falls to the pasteboard path or to a held result; recognition, diarization and rewriting continue to completion. Revocation during recognizing does not stop recognition.
- Input Monitoring denied or revoked: the event tap cannot run, so push-to-talk is unavailable and toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey; an in-flight run continues and the panel gains a stop control.
- Automation for a browser denied: URL predicates do not match, rule evaluation continues, and the panel shows that the mode came from the fallback. Automation for a media player denied: that player's adapter is unavailable, so D-025's owned-pause path is unavailable for it.
- Restoration: capabilities are re-probed on the relevant system notification and at each arming, and the panel reports a recovered capability once instead of on every session.

## Secure input

If IsSecureEventInputEnabled() is true at arming, the run records but is marked delivery-unavailable up front. If it becomes true by delivery time, the app posts no events, holds the result in History, offers copy, and states that another application has secure input active. Password fields are the common case, and silently dropping text there would be the worst available failure.

## Delivery: target, confirmation predicate and ladder (D-008, D-009, D-010)

Exactly one delivery target is defined for each focus outcome, and every later step operates on that target:

- The latched element is still focused: the target is the latched element.
- The latched application is frontmost with a different element focused, and the per-mode follow-focus setting is on, which is the default: the target is the currently focused element, re-resolved at delivery. Confirmation and submission use that element.
- Same application, follow-focus off: no target; hold.
- A different application is frontmost, or the latched application quit: no target; hold, with a card offering Deliver and Copy. Re-activating the latched application first is opt-in, because it steals focus.

Confirmation is a predicate over content, not over length. Before the operation the coordinator records the target's selected range and, where readable, its value. After the operation it re-reads and confirms that the expected text appears at the expected insertion location and that the caret or selection sits immediately after it. Three outcomes follow:

- confirmed: the predicate holds. The attempt is delivered.
- explicit negative: the value is fully readable, is byte-identical to the pre-state, and the selection is unchanged. Only this outcome permits the next rung.
- not evaluable: the target does not expose the readback the predicate needs, or the value changed in a way the predicate cannot attribute. The attempt is unconfirmed. No further rung runs, because posting a paste event carries no acknowledgment that the target consumed the pasteboard, and a second attempt is how a paragraph gets inserted twice.

The ladder: rung 1 sets AXSelectedText on the target, which inserts at the caret or replaces the current selection; the app never sets AXValue, because RESEARCH records that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents. Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V. Rung 3 synthesizes Unicode typing, capped at 400 characters, and runs only after an explicit negative from a fully readable target. Above the cap the app holds and offers copy.

Attempt states and transitions (D-010): pending is committed before any event is posted or any accessibility write is issued; in_progress while a rung is running; delivered on a confirmed predicate; rejected when a rung returns an explicit negative, which is not terminal and hands off to the next rung; unconfirmed when the predicate is not evaluable, which is terminal for the automatic path; held when no target exists or the cap is exceeded; failed on an error before any effect. Terminal states are delivered, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review. At launch, only pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review; delivered, held and failed are left as they are, so a successful past delivery is never re-surfaced. Nothing is ever re-posted automatically; re-delivery is a user action.

Pasteboard handling: snapshot before writing, and restore only after a confirmed delivery and only while changeCount still equals ours, or on the user's explicit Restore clipboard action. There is no timer-based restore, because a delayed consumer can read the pasteboard after any interval the app could pick. After an unconfirmed outcome the transcript stays on the pasteboard and the panel says so, which is the behavior that cannot lose the text. Where the pasteboard cannot be snapshotted, meaning it exceeds the configured snapshot limit or holds promised files or unsupported types, the user is told before anything is written and chooses between proceeding without restore and copy-only.

Submission: the Return is posted after a confirmed delivery to the delivery target when the submit modifier was held at stop, whichever rung achieved it. Posting Return is an event-synthesis operation and does not depend on which mechanism inserted the text. A held, rejected or unconfirmed attempt never auto-submits.

## Service failures (D-003)

A service crash or termination invalidates the connection. The client marks the run failed at its current stage with the exit status, keeps every committed result, releases the job's credit, and offers retry. Three crashes on one model installation mark it suspect in the model list. Because a service holds only loaded models and the current job's window queue, retry reloads from the manifest and needs no state salvage. A service that stops consuming credit is treated as hung after a no-progress interval measured against delivered windows, and is terminated by the client.

## Model and runtime failures (D-022, D-038)

- Download interrupted or hash mismatch: the staging directory is removed, no blob is created, the active installation is untouched, and the error names expected and computed digests.
- User-supplied model failing its per-kind load smoke test: it stays in staging with the error attached and nothing is activated. The smoke test checks that the runtime can load the weights and produce output on a fixed sample; it is a capability check and never a quality judgment, so a compatible model with no benchmark row activates normally and is labeled unmeasured.
- Model blob missing for a pinned run: if the installation is archived, the run is refused up front with an offer to restore the weights by import or download; if the installation claims installed but the blob is gone, the row moves to missing and the same offer appears. Loading never falls back to downloading.
- Pairing exceeding the residency budget: refused at activation with the arithmetic shown, the refusal stating whether the numbers are measured or declared, and the user can override, because it is their machine.

## Resource and storage failures

- Disk full during capture: capture stops, the journal is sealed to the last complete chunk, the recording is marked interrupted, and the panel reports the reason.
- Journal fsync failing repeatedly: capture stops instead of continuing with an unrecoverable tail.
- Unsupported import format: the source is untouched, the session directory is removed, and the error names the format and the optional external decoder path (D-018, D-028).
- Audio device removed mid-run: capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted. The app does not silently switch devices under an active recording.

## Generated text whose compliance cannot be established (D-012)

Checks are divided by what they need. The language-independent set runs on every generation: expansion ratio against the mode's limit, context overlap rejecting any span of eight or more tokens present in the context block and absent from the transcript, vocabulary term survival, and a script sanity check. The language-dependent set needs a validator pack: interrogative survival in order, content-word recall, and detection of sentences with no content-word support in the input.

An observed violation in either set is a contract violation: the run retries once with a stricter instruction, and on a second violation the delivered text is the normalized transcript, the generated text is retained as a result marked contract_violation, and the panel says which check failed. A sentence with no content-word support is treated as a violation on the same path; for a mode whose contract declares summarization, such as meeting notes, the citation requirement governs instead and uncited bullets are dropped.

When the run's language has no pack, the language-dependent checks are unavailable rather than failed. The model still runs and its output is still produced and retained, because pack coverage must not become a restriction on which models a user may use. What changes is the delivered text, and only in the case where the missing check is the one that matters: if the mode declares answersQuestions false and the normalized transcript contains an interrogative marker, the delivered text defaults to the normalized transcript with the generated text one click away in the panel and in History, marked checks_partial. If the transcript contains no interrogative, the generated text is delivered and marked checks_partial with the check list attached. A per-mode setting delivers generated text under partial checks in both cases and records that setting on the result.

For context sources the app does not control, the conservative measure is at the prompt rather than after it: screen text and pasteboard text are distilled to a capped term list by default rather than passed as prose, which removes instruction-shaped sentences from the prompt entirely. Passing them as prose is per-mode opt-in and recorded on the result. Focused-element text is passed as prose, since it is usually the document being written into, and is covered by the checks above.

The claim stops there. These checks are necessary conditions. They can pass on text whose meaning changed, and the adversarial corpus in verification is the standing test of how far they reach.

## Meeting attribution with weak evidence (D-023)

The diarizer supplies cluster boundaries. RESEARCH establishes that its result type exposes speaker centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, that a speaker may have no centroid, and that the declaration does not establish per-segment confidence or margin outputs. The schema follows that exactly: per-segment calibrated confidence is stored as unknown, no per-segment margin is stored, and the only quantitative evidence retained is centroid cosine distance where a centroid exists. Every segment carries attribution_state in {assigned, unverified, assigned_by_user, unattributed}; without per-segment evidence the default is unverified. The transcript shows the cluster label with an unverified marker, and notes attribute only segments whose state is assigned_by_user or assigned. Cross-recording identity is proposed only where both sides have centroids, is always presented for confirmation rather than applied, and is unavailable for a speaker with no centroid, where naming stays per-recording. Segments whose microphone content correlates with delayed system audio are marked probable echo and excluded from microphone-side attribution. A user can assign, merge or split speakers at any time; each edit appends an assignment revision (D-037) and sets attribution_state to assigned_by_user, which no later diarization run overwrites.

## Desktop restore failures (D-025)

Pausing and resuming are treated differently because their evidence differs. Pausing without knowing the recipient is acceptable: the worst case is that nothing was playing. Resuming without knowing the recipient can start audio the user stopped by hand, so automatic resumption happens only through a player integration that names the player and observes its transition from playing to paused. For a player with no adapter, the app may still post a play-pause key when the default output device reports a running client, records the pause as unattributed, and offers Resume playback as an explicit user action for ten minutes; it never resumes such a pause on its own, and no setting enables that. Input device volume is restored only if the current value still equals the value the app set; any mismatch means no restore and a note that the setting was left as found.

## Dependency order among capability areas

- The store, the run state machine, the manifest, the lease protocol and the recovery table depend on nothing external and come first, exercised against fake adapters. Everything else depends on them.
- Capture and delivery depend on the run machine, the recovery contract and the capability matrix (D-006, D-031, D-032). Neither depends on a model, so both can be accepted before any runtime is integrated.
- Recognition depends on capture and on the model store, because a run pins a model installation (D-022).
- Vocabulary and the Standard mode depend on recognition. Generation modes depend on vocabulary, on the check set and packs (D-012) and on F2, which governs how the generation service is launched.
- Automatic mode selection and context depend on modes existing and on the permission matrix for their degraded states.
- System audio and file import depend on the ingest port and on the memory slope from F1, which tells the credit window how much a service will hold.
- Meetings depend on system-audio and file capture, on F5, on the diarization service placement (D-003) and on the acquisition path for weights the application does not bundle. The assignment-revision schema (D-037) depends on F5's field inventory.
- Languages and retention depend on results and leases already existing; translation is a result kind and retention is a deletion job under the same protocol (D-033).
- Desktop integration depends on capture and delivery only; the player adapters (D-025) are independent of everything else.

## Acceptance evidence by area

Each area is accepted on evidence approved by the owner named in D-035, against behavior tables written before the tests.

- Store and run machine: the recovery outcome for every non-terminal state, including diarizing and noting, asserted after a kill at that state boundary, matching the approved table.
- Capture: the measured loss bound from F3 within its approved range, plus a decodable artifact with a packet count matching the durable index prefix after every injected kill.
- Delivery: the dated application matrix from F4, automated permission-matrix tests, the full attempt-state transition table exercised including the equal-length replacement case, and a crash-during-delivery test showing needs_review with no re-post.
- Recognition: word error rate rows attached to machine, model revision and quantization, plus the memory slope at three durations measured inside the service.
- Vocabulary: table-driven determinism across ordering, boundaries, case and scripts without spaces.
- Modes: human rubric scores on the fidelity corpus including adversarial cases, scored under the rule in verification, plus per-mode violation and checks_partial rates.
- Models: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction, activation while a run holds a lease, an import with no benchmark row that activates and is labeled unmeasured, archive and restore of an installation with History rows still resolving, and a complete session with the network denied.
- Mode rules and context: a dated browser URL matrix, rule-shadowing tests, and tests that screen and pasteboard context reach the prompt as a term list unless the mode opts into prose.
- Input sources: resident size at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours in both processes with the fitted slope reported, and a failed import leaving its source byte-identical.
- Meetings: two-stream alignment drift, diarization error rate on a labeled internal set, the share of segments carrying unknown confidence, and provenance tests showing that renaming a speaker or re-running diarization leaves an existing note's text and pinned inputs unchanged while History flags the drift.
- History: deletion and retention race tests against live leases, and provenance tests over two recognition runs and two diarization runs of one recording.
- Desktop: a manual matrix over a music player, a browser tab and a video conferencing application, recording which had an adapter, what paused, what resumed automatically and what required the user action.

## Adding a new input source

A new source implements AudioSource, emitting timestamped native frames plus a SourceDescriptor giving live or seekable, clock domain, known duration, native rate and channel layout, and whether it honors credit. Only arming branches on live against seekable, because a live source latches a delivery target and a file source does not. The alternative considered was a pipeline per source, each owning its chunking, conversion and cancellation. That is shorter today and duplicates the parts most likely to be wrong: a memory bug on long input would exist only in the import path, and cancellation semantics would drift between paths. The cost of one port is that every source carries timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift.

## Replacing a model runtime

Runtimes are separate adapter targets and separate service binaries, each publishing a capability descriptor with measured fields and a parameter schema. results.params_json stores parameters under a stable application-level schema with a runtime-specific extension blob, and results.params_rendered stores the human-readable form produced at insert time, so History rows from a removed runtime stay readable even after its presentation hook is gone. The settings interface renders common parameters, meaning context length, temperature, beam size, thread count and quantization, generically from that schema, and a runtime may supply presentation hooks for parameters with conditional validity, model-specific ranges or memory effects. Replacing a runtime therefore adds a bounded amount of interface work; a claim that a schema removes bespoke interface work entirely would be too strong.

Storage effect of a swap is bounded by D-038 rather than by garbage collection alone. History results reference their installations permanently, so an installation row is never unreferenced and collection by reference count would retain every old multi-gigabyte model forever. Archiving separates the two: the row, hashes, capabilities and notices stay, the weights are released, and History states that reprocessing through that installation is unavailable until the weights are restored. The model manager shows per-runtime totals for installed weights and offers archiving of a whole runtime's installations when its adapter is removed.

Calling a runtime API directly from feature code removes a layer. Under that arrangement, swapping runtimes touches every call site, the settings interface and the persisted parameters, and old History rows referencing removed parameter names become uninterpretable. RESEARCH flags long-recording behavior and integration cost as unexamined for both speech candidates, so designing as though the first choice is permanent would be the wrong bet.

## Maintenance costs accepted

- GRDB: a dependency with its own release cadence plus migration discipline, paid for by FTS5 and tested migrations.
- Vendored C and C++ runtimes: long builds, periodic vendoring and upstream API drift. Pinned to tagged revisions with an update checklist that reruns the evaluation harness and refreshes capability descriptors.
- CGEventTap and accessibility insertion: per-application behavior is undocumented and changes. The delivery matrix is re-run per macOS minor release and per major update of the applications in it, and the result is a dated table in the repository.
- Player adapters (D-025): one integration per supported player, each with its own automation permission and its own breakage risk on player updates. Players without an adapter keep the manual resume action, so the failure mode of an unmaintained adapter is a lost convenience.
- Validator language packs: each language needs segmentation, interrogative detection and a content-word list, plus rubric review in that language. Languages without a pack run the language-independent set and take the disposition in D-012.
- Chunk journal: extra file management, two fsyncs per chunk period and a sealer to maintain. It buys a recovery story that does not depend on a container surviving a kill.
- XPC services: five bundles to sign, entitlement sets to keep correct, and interruption handling in the client. A missing entitlement fails closed, which is the direction worth paying for.

## What supporting other Macs would require

Intel support means the whisper.cpp adapter with its own model format, a smaller generation model, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run; RESEARCH notes that documented platform support does not establish comparable performance. Machines with 8 GB need a smaller pairing and a residency policy that unloads the speech model before loading the generation model, at the cost of latency between stages, and diarization would not run beside either. Both are adapter and policy changes and neither touches the store or the run machine.

## Who decides what correct means (D-035)

A passing test shows the implementation met its assertions under the tested conditions; the assertions can encode a wrong expectation. Expected behavior is therefore written and approved before tests are written. docs/behavior/ holds a table per subsystem giving, for each state and event pair, the expected next state, the persisted effect and the user-visible effect. Cancellation at every stage, permission loss per capability, focus change, crash at each boundary, lease conflict, service interruption, delivery attempt transitions and check disposition are events in those tables. Every row cites a SPEC.md clause; rows with no clause are marked derived and need explicit approval. The normative approver is the user as product owner, or a delegate named in docs/behavior/OWNERS; independent authorship is a hygiene rule and carries no authority. Tests reference row identifiers, and changing an approved row requires re-approval recorded in git history. The same approver signs the acceptance ranges below before the corresponding gate runs.

- Provenance tests: re-recognize a recording under a second speech model and re-diarize it, then generate notes from each combination, and assert that every artifact resolves to exactly one transcript, one diarization result, one assignment revision and one model installation per stage.
- Meeting provenance drift: generate notes, rename a speaker, re-run diarization, and assert the note text and its pinned inputs are unchanged while History reports the drift and offers regeneration.
- Crash injection: SIGKILL at each stage boundary, including diarizing and noting, relaunch, and assert the recovery outcome named in the approved table, including no automatic re-delivery after a kill during delivering and idempotent re-sealing after a kill during sealing.
- Pre-commit disposition: cancel during arming, capturing and sealing, kill the process before the sweep, relaunch, and assert the manifest disposition determines the outcome with no orphaned session directory.
- Kill-at-offset capture experiment (F3): randomized kills during capture across chunk boundaries and both fsync points, measuring the maximum lost interval and asserting that the rebuilt packet table decodes end to end with a packet count matching the durable index prefix. It has not been run.

## Human review where assertions are weak

Transformation fidelity is reviewed and not only asserted. A fixed corpus of 40 recordings per mode per shipped language has expected outputs, scored against five criteria: meaning preserved, no invented facts, questions still questions, vocabulary terms intact, formatting within the declared contract. Each criterion is scored 0, 1 or 2 against a written definition of each level. Two reviewers score independently, neither being the author of the mode under review; where they differ by more than one point on any criterion a third reviewer adjudicates and that score stands. The ship rule for a built-in mode revision: no item may score 0 on meaning preserved, no invented facts, or questions still questions; at most two items may score 1 on any criterion; and the mean across all criteria and items is at least 1.8. A revision that fails is revised and re-scored; a built-in that cannot meet the rule is not shipped as a built-in and the reason is recorded. The corpus includes adversarial cases built to pass lexical checks while changing meaning: removed or inserted negation, swapped quantities, modality changes such as must to may, swapped attribution between two named people, an answer appended after a retained question, and a sentence copied from the context block. The product owner approves the expected outputs and the rule.

Meeting notes are scored on the same scale with citation validity checked automatically and the uncited-bullet drop rate tracked; a note whose bullets cite segments that do not support them scores 0 on no invented facts.

Practical behavior in other macOS applications is verified by running the delivery matrix by hand across TextEdit, Mail, Notes, Safari plain input and contenteditable, Chrome, Xcode, Terminal, VS Code, Slack, Messages and Figma. Each cell records whether rung 1 is supported and preserved existing field content; whether the confirmation predicate is evaluable; insertion at a caret in the middle of existing text; replacement of an active selection with equal-length and different-length text; paste with a delayed consumer; pasteboard state after an unconfirmed outcome; non-Latin text covering Japanese, Arabic in a right-to-left field, combining marks and emoji; behavior with an input method active; secure fields; and focus changing while events are being posted. The table is dated and re-run on macOS updates.

## Measurement protocols, acceptance ranges and actions

No benchmark here has been executed. Each protocol is defined so that results, when they exist, are attributable, and each carries the range that would keep the shipped default and the action if it does not. These ranges govern development choices about defaults; they never gate a compatible model the user imports.

- F1 recognition: word error rate by language on a public set and an internal 60-utterance set, recording machine model, memory, macOS version, runtime revision, model revision and quantization. Retention range: the default installation is no more than 15 percent relative worse than the fallback adapter running an equivalent model on the same audio. Action on failure: build the whisper.cpp adapter and re-select the default pairing.
- F1 latency: stop to final transcript for a 30-second utterance, p50 at most 3.0 s and p95 at most 6.0 s on the evaluation target, reported as a distribution over at least 20 runs. Action on failure: change the default model size or quantization first; if no default meets it, publish the measured figure and drop the target rather than concealing it.
- F1 memory: peak service resident size at 3 hours no more than the 10-minute peak plus 500 MB. Action on failure: reduce the credit window and re-measure; if the slope persists, imports move to the fallback adapter.
- F1 descriptors: cancellation latency at p50 and p95, transcript equivalence after preemption and resume, peak service resident size and Metal heap peak per model installation. Absence of verified checkpoint equivalence keeps whole-job restart (D-004).
- F3 capture: maximum lost interval at most 4 seconds across at least 200 randomized kills, and every recovery decoding end to end. Action on failure: shorten the chunk period to 1 second and re-measure; if reconstruction is invalid at any period, adopt the retain-until-verified fallback in D-030.
- F5 diarization inventory: the field list, centroid availability per fixture, and segmenter and embedder resident size and wall time. No pass or fail; the result sets the meeting schema and the residency numbers. If centroids are unavailable for a speaker, cross-recording naming for that speaker is offered only as a user action.
- Diarization quality: diarization error rate on a labeled internal meeting set, the share of segments carrying unknown confidence, whether centroid distance is monotone with correctness on cross-recording pairs, and behavior under speaker echo without headphones. This is reported, not a ship gate, because the feature ships with manual assignment and unverified marking either way; a monotonicity result would allow a derived threshold with its calibration curve recorded.
- Two-stream alignment: drift between microphone and system streams over a long meeting, measured against injected reference tones.

Until a measurement exists, the interface reports language support as declared by the model publisher and marked unmeasured, and no latency claim appears in the product.

Basis: content-word recall, interrogative survival, expansion ratio and context n-gram overlap can all pass on text whose meaning changed. Reconsider if the adversarial fidelity corpus finds a class of violations that survives every check, which would argue for a sampled semantic check by a second model despite its cost and its shared failure mode.

Leaving the dictated transcript on the pasteboard after an unconfirmed delivery is preferable to restoring the previous contents on a timer. Basis: the prior review established that any fixed delay races a delayed consumer, and losing the user's text is worse than leaving the pasteboard changed; the panel states the pasteboard holds the transcript and offers Restore clipboard. Reconsider if F4 shows a target class where consumption can be confirmed, which lets restore run automatically for those targets.

A CoreAudio device-is-running flag on the default output device is an adequate trigger for offering to pause media and is not evidence of ownership of any pause. Basis: it is a public property needing no private framework, and it identifies neither the playing application nor the effect of a posted media key. That is why automatic resumption is confined to player adapters that name the player and observe its transition. Reconsider if a supported system API supplies target identity and pause confirmation without a per-player integration.

AVFoundation covers the initial import format matrix: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v and mov. Basis: system decoder coverage. Reconsider at the first refusal, with opus in webm or matroska the likely ones, at which point the user-selected external decoder running inside the sandboxed decode service is the documented path.

FTS5 is compiled into the system SQLite on the deployment baseline. Basis: it has shipped enabled for several macOS releases, though this is a build-setup check and not a verified fact here. Reconsider immediately if the check fails; the fallback is GRDB against a bundled SQLite, which increases binary size and adds an update obligation.

Separate microphone and system-audio streams give better attribution than diarizing a mixed stream, and channel origin is a fact about capture instead of a claim about who spoke. Basis: structural, since the two capture paths exist and channel origin is certain, while echo from speakers into the microphone is not accounted for by structure alone. Reconsider after diarization and echo evaluation; if a mixed-stream diarizer performs comparably, the second stream becomes an optimization.

The diarizer supplies cluster boundaries and centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, supplies no per-segment confidence or margin, and may supply no centroid for a given speaker. Basis: stated in RESEARCH for SpeakerKit v1.1.0's DiarizationResult declaration, from source inspection with no inference experiment run. The schema therefore stores per-segment calibrated confidence as unknown, stores no per-segment margin, and uses centroid distance only for cross-recording identity proposals that the user confirms. Reconsider at F5, which inventories the fields actually exposed at the pinned version, and after evaluation shows whether centroid distance is monotone with correctness.

Lossless 16 kHz mono audio at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour makes indefinite dictation retention acceptable by default, while native-rate meeting streams are large enough to surface in the library size view. Basis: arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour and typical lossless ratios. Reconsider when a library crosses a user-visible size threshold, at which point the retention interface is surfaced instead of a default quietly applied.

A 200 ms arming budget is tolerable for mode resolution and context sampling, and context sources missing it are skipped for that run. Basis: a design choice about perceived responsiveness with no user study; audio capture no longer waits on it because the pre-roll ring starts at the trigger, so the budget affects context completeness rather than lost speech. Reconsider if screen-context sampling routinely misses the deadline and users want it, which moves sampling off the arming path and makes the rewrite stage wait for it.

The pasteboard snapshot limit of 10 MB is a starting value, not a measured threshold. Basis: chosen to avoid duplicating large images and file promises in memory during a latency-sensitive operation, with no measurement of snapshot cost. It is a configurable setting, and F4 records snapshot time by content type so the default can be set from data. Reconsider once that measurement exists.

Weights the application offers for download are limited to assets whose notices permit redistribution, and everything else is user-imported. Basis: RESEARCH records the WhisperKit model card as MIT and records component-specific notices for the diarization collection referring to WeSpeaker and VBx. Reconsider per asset as the notice inventory is compiled; an asset that cannot be offered stays importable, so no feature depends on the outcome.

decisions.title: macOS baseline and hardware target
decisions.choice: Deployment target macOS 14.0 and Apple Silicon for the first release, with later-OS APIs gated at runtime and never required.
decisions.rationale: The speech runtime selected in D-020 and the diarizer in D-023 ship in one Swift package whose prerequisites RESEARCH records as macOS 14 and Xcode 16, so the floor follows a dependency the design has committed to. ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture is available at 14; the WWDC24 microphone stream output arrived later, and microphone capture uses AVAudioEngine on every supported version, so the newer output is off the critical path. Apple Silicon only in the first release is an engineering decision, not a reading of the specification: a second architecture requires its own model format, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run, and doing that before the primary target has any measurement spends effort on a comparison neither side of which is known.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 15 for the unified ScreenCaptureKit microphone and system-audio stream
alternatives.tradeoff: One capture path and a shared clock for meetings, at the cost of excluding Sonoma users for a convenience the two-stream design handles with host-time alignment.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 13
alternatives.tradeoff: Wider reach; falls below the selected package's stated prerequisite and adds an operating system to the support matrix that nothing is evaluated on.

alternatives.option: Ship Intel and Apple Silicon together
alternatives.tradeoff: Broader hardware coverage; doubles the evaluation burden that RESEARCH warns documentation cannot substitute for, and forces a second model tier before the primary target is measured.

decisions.consequences: Meetings align two streams by host time instead of receiving them from one. Intel users wait for the second speech adapter and its own evaluation, and the reason is recorded here rather than attributed to the specification. Any API newer than 14 sits behind an availability check with a defined fallback, and the availability matrix is part of the capture behavior tables.
decisions.reconsider_when: The Argmax dependency is dropped, measured two-stream drift forces a single-stream capture path, or an Intel requirement is confirmed.

decisions.title: Package layout and dependency direction
decisions.choice: One SPM package with a pure core, a ports target of protocols and value types, a validation target holding transformation contracts and language packs, adapter targets per external concern, service targets for inference, and a thin Xcode app shell as the composition root. Core depends only on ports; nothing depends on an adapter except the shell.
decisions.rationale: The scope includes a speech runtime that may be replaced, four input sources, a diarizer, and an insertion mechanism whose behavior varies per target application. Each is an adapter. Keeping the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline and contract checking free of system frameworks is what lets the earliest work exercise cancel, crash, delete-during-processing and retention races before any runtime exists. Service logic living in library targets keeps it inside swift test even though the bundles are produced by Xcode.

alternatives.option: Single application target with feature folders
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster early progress; every behavioral test then needs permissions and real models, and swapping a runtime touches feature code throughout.

alternatives.option: Separate SPM packages per subsystem in a workspace
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger boundaries and independent versioning, at the cost of cross-package version churn for a single application with one consumer.

decisions.consequences: Adapters need explicit wiring in the shell and value types at the boundary in place of framework types passed around. The application bundle cannot come from swift build alone, so there are two entry points: swift test for logic and the Xcode scheme for the shipping application and its signed services.
decisions.reconsider_when: The port boundary starts needing per-adapter escape hatches that leak framework types into core, which would mean the abstraction is fighting the domain.

decisions.title: Inference runs in bundled sandboxed XPC services, one per model kind
decisions.choice: Speech recognition, generation, diarization and optional external decoding each run in a bundled XPC service, sandboxed on its own with com.apple.security.network.client withheld, reached over its XPC connection. Model weights arrive as opened file descriptors or through a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs. No inference runs in the app process and nothing listens on a port.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH's follow-up records that bundled services have separate sandboxes, that a service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, and that signed services with network entitlements withheld are the thing to evaluate for inference; it also states that a scan for socket symbols cannot establish that a process lacks network access. A withheld entitlement is a property of the process, so it covers linked frameworks and dynamically loaded code that a scan cannot reach. Diarization gets its own service rather than sharing SpeechService for two reasons: RESEARCH records that this runtime's default initialization may download models, making it the component whose acquisition control most needs an enforced boundary, and it loads a different model set whose residency must be counted separately from the speech model's single-slot rule. Crash isolation and per-process residency accounting apply to all four.

alternatives.option: Child helper processes over an inherited socket pair
alternatives.tradeoff: Full control of launch and lifecycle with no launchd involvement; provides no system-level egress denial, so the offline claim reduces to the symbol scan RESEARCH rejects as evidence.

alternatives.option: Link the runtimes into the application process
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest latency and no serialization boundary; a native crash kills the app mid-run and address-space growth from model loading persists for the process lifetime.

alternatives.option: Run diarization inside SpeechService
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer bundle to sign and one connection to manage; couples two model sets in one residency slot and gives the runtime with the documented implicit-download behavior the same process as the one without it.

alternatives.option: Run the upstream HTTP server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling and its API; opens a port every local process can reach and turns the offline property into a claim about configuration the app does not own.

decisions.consequences: Connection interruption is a normal event: the run fails at its stage, committed results stand, and the next admission rebuilds the service. Audio windows cross the connection under credit, so the memory ceiling is measured in each service as well as the app. Model file access needs descriptors or a path exception, settled by F2. Five bundles are signed with their own entitlement sets, and a missing entitlement fails closed.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows a sandboxed service cannot load the chosen runtimes by either access mechanism, or IPC overhead measurably dominates generation latency for short dictations.

decisions.title: Concurrency model, lane structure and scheduling from measured runtime capabilities
decisions.choice: One actor per processing run owning its state and rows; a real-time audio callback writing into lock-free rings; a single ResourceScheduler actor with a capture lane, an interactive lane and a batch lane. The capture writer and the incremental sealer are not model-bound and are not admitted: they run on the capture lane above batch quality of service with no admission gate. Model slots are counted per kind, at most one speech, one generation and one diarization model set resident, with admission also checking the summed footprint against D-027. Preemption is read from each runtime's measured capability descriptor: yield and resume only where the descriptor records verified checkpoint equivalence, otherwise cancel and restart the whole job, or let it finish behind a displayed bound.
decisions.rationale: The scope puts a latency-sensitive dictation path beside long batch work on a machine that cannot hold several models resident, so an admission policy is needed and is better in one testable place than invented by the first task that hits contention. Putting the sealer in the batch lane would let a three-hour import starve the component that keeps the journal window bounded during live capture, so it is exempt from admission entirely. Nothing in RESEARCH establishes that either runtime can checkpoint and resume without changing output, so restarting from a checkpoint is used only where the descriptor establishes equivalence, and whole-job restart is the default because it is correct without that evidence.

alternatives.option: Unstructured concurrency with a global lock around model access
alternatives.tradeoff: Less code; priority inversion when a three-hour import holds the lock while the user dictates, with no clean preemption point.

alternatives.option: Serial queue, first come first served
alternatives.tradeoff: Predictable; the user waits behind a batch job, which is the failure the requirements care about most.

alternatives.option: Admit the sealer as batch work like any other job
alternatives.tradeoff: One admission path for everything; the journal window becomes a function of batch queue depth, which breaks the storage bound the capture design depends on.

alternatives.option: Concurrent residency of every model kind with no admission control
alternatives.tradeoff: Better pipelining on a large machine; on the 16 GB target it invites swap, turning a latency problem into a system-wide stall.

decisions.consequences: Batch workers need restart points even under the default policy. The provisional pass is an admitted job that can be denied, so the panel has a reduced-preview state rather than a stalled transcript (D-011). The audio callback thread has hard constraints that need review discipline. Descriptor values become shipped data refreshed when a runtime is updated. Diarization competes with recognition and generation for the budget rather than being invisible to it.
decisions.reconsider_when: Descriptors show a runtime whose resume reproduces the unpreempted transcript, allowing true preemption, or measurements show a machine class where concurrent residency fits and the per-kind single-slot rule costs latency for nothing.

decisions.title: Persistence: SQLite with FTS5 for metadata and text, files for audio
decisions.choice: SQLite through GRDB in WAL mode for metadata, runs, results, leases and result text, with FTS5 over result text; audio in per-recording directories. Numbered migrations with fixture-based migration tests.
decisions.rationale: History requires search across transcripts and results, and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is the reason to prefer SQLite. Deletion during active work, lease acquisition and model activation all need a transaction that combines a check with a write. Keeping audio out of the database keeps its backup, integrity check and migration times short.

alternatives.option: SwiftData
alternatives.tradeoff: Least code for models and views with native observation; no full-text index, and migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures for a schema that must survive many capability additions.

alternatives.option: Core Data with an external search index
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature and Apple-supported; adds a second index to keep consistent with deletions, which is the consistency problem the tombstone and lease rules exist to contain.

alternatives.option: Raw libsqlite3 with a hand-written wrapper
alternatives.tradeoff: No third-party dependency; reimplements migrations, statement caching and observation, which is where maintenance accumulates.

alternatives.option: JSON files per recording with an in-memory index
