decisions.reconsider_when: Lease contention delays retention long enough to matter, which would argue for pausing playback and preempting batch work in place of deferring.

decisions.title: Measurements precede the boundaries they can invalidate, with approved acceptance ranges
decisions.choice: Five evidence gates (F1 runtime harness, F2 service isolation, F3 kill-at-offset capture, F4 insertion matrix, F5 diarizer adapter inventory) run before the boundaries that depend on them. Each gate's acceptance range and the action attached to a failure are approved under D-035 before it runs, as listed in verification. These ranges govern shipped defaults; none of them gates a compatible model a user imports. The design records ordering constraints, dependencies and acceptance evidence per capability area; the task-level phase breakdown is produced after this design is accepted.
decisions.rationale: Several decisions depend on properties nothing has measured: how the chosen runtime behaves on long input and under cancellation, whether a sandboxed service can load models and is denied the network, how much audio a crash costs, which applications allow confirmable insertion, and which fields the diarizer actually exposes. Scheduling those after the ports and schema that depend on them would mean a negative result invalidates work already built on it. Recording a range and an action beforehand is what makes the result decide something; a measurement with no attached consequence is a number in a report. Each gate has a fallback that satisfies the requirement it touches, so a negative result changes a parameter or an adapter and not the architecture.

alternatives.option: Start the skeleton immediately and measure later
alternatives.tradeoff: Visible progress sooner; a negative F1, F3 or F5 result forces rework of the ingest port, the scheduler, the capture writer or the meeting schema.

alternatives.option: Run the gates but decide acceptance after seeing the numbers
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids arguing about thresholds in advance; invites fitting the threshold to the result, which removes the gate's purpose.

alternatives.option: Prototype everything end to end before designing
alternatives.tradeoff: Maximum evidence before commitment; delays every requirement that does not depend on the unknowns.

alternatives.option: Treat the unknowns as risks accepted at implementation time
alternatives.tradeoff: No gates to schedule; hands behavioral decisions to whichever task hits them, which the specification forbids.

decisions.consequences: Some work produces evidence instead of shippable behavior: descriptors, matrices, bounds, field inventories and decision updates. Gate outputs feed D-001, D-004, D-009, D-011, D-020, D-023, D-027, D-028, D-030 and D-037, so those decisions carry conservative defaults until the evidence lands. Approving ranges before the work adds a decision point to the schedule.
decisions.reconsider_when: A gate's fallback proves acceptable enough that the measurement is not worth its cost, which is a judgment to record instead of assume.

decisions.title: Named approval authority, specification traceability, and approved acceptance ranges
decisions.choice: Expected behavior lives in docs/behavior/ tables whose rows each cite a SPEC.md clause or are marked derived. The normative approver is the user as product owner, or a delegate named in docs/behavior/OWNERS. The same approver signs each gate's acceptance range and failure action before that gate runs, and the rubric scoring rule before the fidelity corpus is scored. Approval of a table gates writing tests against it; tests reference row identifiers; changing an approved row requires re-approval recorded in git history. Independent authorship of tables is a hygiene rule and carries no authority.
decisions.rationale: A passing test proves only that the code met its assertions, so the assertions need an owner who can say they are the intended product behavior. The previous revision established who approves behavior rows but left the measurement gates with no stated pass condition, so a number could arrive with nobody obliged to say what it meant; ranges and actions are now part of what gets approved. Clause citations make it possible to check that a requirement was followed into the design instead of paraphrased.

alternatives.option: Peer review by any team member
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheap and fast; two people can share the same misreading of a requirement with nobody empowered to settle it.

alternatives.option: Approve behavior tables but leave measurement thresholds to engineering
alternatives.tradeoff: Less product-owner time; the thresholds that decide which runtime and which defaults ship would then have no product authority behind them.

alternatives.option: Treat SPEC.md as the only source and skip behavior tables
alternatives.tradeoff: No second artifact to maintain; the specification does not enumerate state and event pairs, so implementers fill the gaps silently.

alternatives.option: Derive expectations from the implementation and review the diff
alternatives.tradeoff: Least documentation work; makes the code its own specification, which is the failure this decision exists to prevent.

decisions.consequences: Capability areas cannot be accepted until their tables are approved, and gates cannot run until their ranges are, which puts the product owner on the critical path twice. Derived rows are visible as a category, so the volume of behavior with no specification basis stays measurable.
decisions.reconsider_when: Approval becomes the dominant delay, which would argue for pre-approved templates for mechanical tables instead of removing the gate.

decisions.title: Distribution: direct Developer ID distribution, ad hoc signing for local builds
decisions.choice: The application ships outside the Mac App Store, notarized under a Developer ID certificate with the hardened runtime, as an unsandboxed shell containing sandboxed XPC services. Local development builds may be ad hoc signed. App Store submission is not planned.
decisions.rationale: This is settled here rather than left as a blocking question because the specification already decides it in substance: it asks for direct distribution for this worked example, and it requires a consuming session-level event tap with key-up for push-to-talk (D-026) and setting selected text in another application's accessibility element (D-009). Neither is available to a sandboxed App Store build, so the alternative would not satisfy requirements the specification names. Leaving the question open while the architecture assumed the answer was the contradiction the last review identified.

alternatives.option: Mac App Store distribution
alternatives.tradeoff: System-managed updates and a familiar install path; the sandbox removes push-to-talk and accessibility insertion as specified, so Text delivery and Recording controls would have to be rewritten rather than adapted.

alternatives.option: Unsigned distribution
alternatives.tradeoff: No certificate cost; Gatekeeper blocks casual installation and every TCC grant becomes fragile, which harms exactly the permissions this application depends on.

alternatives.option: Both an App Store build and a direct build
alternatives.tradeoff: Reach plus capability; two feature sets, two permission models and two test matrices for one application.

decisions.consequences: Updates need their own mechanism, and the project carries certificate management and a notarization step in release packaging. Ad hoc signed local builds have an unstable code identity, so TCC grants for Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording and Automation are re-requested after rebuilds; developers keep a stably signed build for permission-dependent work, and this is documented rather than discovered. The entitlement sets in D-003 and D-028 are available precisely because the build is not App Store sandboxed.
decisions.reconsider_when: A product decision requires App Store presence, which would require revising the Text delivery and Recording controls requirements first, since the specified behavior is not implementable under that sandbox.

decisions.title: Speaker assignments as content-addressed revisions, pinned by the notes that used them
decisions.choice: A diarization result is immutable. The mapping from segment to named speaker lives in speaker_assignment_revisions with an append-only chain per recording, each revision content-addressed over its assignments and naming the diarization result it applies to. Identity display names are append-only in speaker_identity_names. A notes run pins the transcript result id, the diarization result id, the assignment revision id and the identity-name set hash in its manifest and records the first three in result_inputs. History compares pinned identifiers against current state and reports drift with a regenerate action.
decisions.rationale: Notes are the one artifact in this design whose meaning depends on user-editable data, so the snapshot rule that D-006 applies to mode settings has to extend to speaker assignments and names. Without a revision, renaming a speaker or re-running diarization would change how a saved note reads while its recorded provenance stayed identical, which is the failure the requirement about later edits not changing saved results describes. Content addressing makes a revision comparable across runs, and keeping names append-only means the transcript view can show what a note saw at generation time rather than what is current.

alternatives.option: Mutable assignments with no revisions
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest editing model and no extra rows; a note's provenance stops describing the data that produced it as soon as a name changes.

alternatives.option: Copy the assignment into the notes result params
alternatives.tradeoff: One place to look and no join; the copy is not comparable to current state, so History cannot tell the user what changed.

alternatives.option: Regenerate notes automatically when assignments change
alternatives.tradeoff: Notes always current; silently replaces text the user may have relied on and spends model time on every rename.

alternatives.option: Version the diarization result itself on every edit
alternatives.tradeoff: One versioned object instead of two; conflates model output with user judgment, so a re-run of the model would appear to overwrite user edits.

decisions.consequences: Every speaker edit writes a revision, so a meeting with heavy editing accumulates rows; they are small and are deleted with the recording. History gains a drift indicator on notes and a regenerate action. Assignment revisions must be reconciled when a new diarization run produces different segment boundaries, which is handled by carrying assigned_by_user states forward where segments overlap and marking the rest unattributed.
decisions.reconsider_when: F5 shows segment identifiers are not stable enough across runs for overlap-based carry-forward, which would need a time-range mapping instead.

decisions.title: Model installation lifecycle states bound storage when a runtime is replaced
decisions.choice: model_installations carries a lifecycle state in {installed, archived, missing}. Archiving releases the weight blobs while retaining the row, the set and per-asset hashes, declared capabilities, per-asset licenses and notices. History results keep referencing archived installations and render from results.params_rendered, and the detail view states that reprocessing through that installation needs the weights restored by import or download. Garbage collection removes a blob when no installed row references it and no lease is live. The model manager offers archiving per installation and for every installation of a runtime whose adapter is being removed. A pinned run against an archived installation is refused up front with a restore offer.
decisions.rationale: Reference counting alone cannot bound storage here, because History results reference their installations permanently by design, so no installation row is ever unreferenced and no weights would ever be collectible; successive runtime replacements would accumulate every old model. Separating what must persist for attribution, which is small, from what must persist for execution, which is gigabytes, is what makes the specification's bounded-storage requirement for replacing a runtime achievable without breaking provenance. Refusing up front rather than failing mid-run keeps the archived state from looking like corruption.

alternatives.option: Retain weights for any installation any result references
alternatives.tradeoff: Reprocessing always available; storage grows without bound across runtime replacements, which the requirement rules out.

alternatives.option: Delete the installation row with the weights
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest cleanup; old History rows lose the identity, licenses and parameters that made them attributable.

alternatives.option: Archive automatically by age or size
alternatives.tradeoff: No user decision needed; removes the ability to reprocess without warning, so archiving stays an explicit action with a size figure attached.

decisions.consequences: A third installation state appears in the model manager and in History, and users must understand that an archived model is attributable but not runnable. Restoring requires the same weights by hash, which the archived row makes checkable. Missing is distinguished from archived so an unexpected disappearance is reported as an error rather than as a user choice.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users archive and restore the same installations repeatedly, which would argue for a compressed local cache of recent weights instead of full release.

coverage.explanation: Global toggle and push-to-talk from another application come from one session-level event tap that observes key-up and consumes the hotkey (D-026), which is available because of the distribution decision recorded in D-036. Toggle and push-to-talk are separate configurable bindings, so a press has one meaning and no hold window is ambiguous; per-mode bindings select a mode and start a run in one action, with conflict detection at bind time. A lost key-up is recovered from tap-disabled and screen-lock notifications and from polling the physical key state, so there is no maximum hold and no recording-duration cap. Capture starts at the trigger into a pre-roll ring while arming work runs concurrently (D-006), so a push-to-talk user who speaks immediately does not lose the first word; the residual device-start latency is measured by the leading-audio test. Without Accessibility or Input Monitoring the tap cannot run, so toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey and push-to-talk is unavailable with an explanation instead of failing silently (D-032). Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage a run can occupy, including sealing, diarizing and noting (D-007), because those are explicit run states (D-006), and a crash mid-run resolves through the state-indexed recovery contract, which now covers the same stage set (D-031).

The processed transcript is inserted at the caret or over the current selection by setting AXSelectedText on the delivery target; the app never sets an element's whole value, so existing field contents survive (D-009), following the distinction RESEARCH draws between an accessibility object's value and its selected text. D-008 names exactly one target for each focus outcome, so policy and mechanism no longer disagree: the latched element when it is still focused, the currently focused element when the latched application is frontmost and follow-focus is on, and no target, meaning hold with Deliver and Copy, in every other case including a departed application. Confirmation is a predicate over content rather than length: the expected text at the expected location with the caret after it. That is what makes an equal-length replacement a success rather than a false rejection, and it yields three outcomes, of which only an explicit negative from a fully readable target permits the next rung; anything unreadable or ambiguous ends as unconfirmed with no retry, because posting a paste event carries no acknowledgment of consumption. Optional submission posts Return after a confirmed delivery to the target when the modifier was held at stop, on whichever rung achieved it, so the preferred accessibility path supports submission too. Clipboard changes are handled by snapshotting before writing and restoring only after confirmed delivery while the change count is ours, or on the user's action; there is no timer, so a delayed consumer cannot race a restore, and after an unconfirmed outcome the transcript stays on the clipboard and the panel says so. Permissions denied or revoked route the result to History and the pasteboard through the capability matrix instead of ending the run (D-032), and secure input suppresses synthesis entirely. Duplicate delivery is prevented structurally: the attempt row commits before any effect, the state table has an explicit terminal delivered state, and only pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review at launch, never re-posted (D-010).

A provisional live transcript comes from a separate pass over a sliding window and a waveform is drawn from a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope computed allocation-free on the capture thread (D-011). The compact window is a non-activating, borderless panel at status-bar level that joins all spaces, is movable by its background and never becomes key, so showing it cannot break the delivery latch. Placement is remembered as a fraction of the display's visible frame plus the display identifier and is clamped to the primary display when either is gone. Provisional text renders in a secondary style with a live label and is replaced by the final transcript with a change highlight; the provisional stream is never persisted as a result, because it was produced over partial context and is a different artifact from the recognition result the run commits (D-006). Recording and processing failures appear as a panel row with a short reason and one action. When the full provisional pass is too expensive or the scheduler denies it while batch work holds the speech model (D-004), the preview degrades through a ladder that still shows text: a smaller dedicated preview model, then batched updates at voice-activity pauses. Dropping to waveform-only is rejected as a fallback because provisional text is a named requirement; if no rung meets the measured bars on the evaluation target, that goes to the product owner as a release question rather than being quietly removed.

Four built-in modes cover ordinary dictation and task-specific output: Standard, Email, Note and Meeting notes (D-013). Each carries a structured transformation contract instead of a prose description. Standard is limited to punctuation, capitalization, optional disfluency removal and vocabulary substitution; Email adds template salutation and sign-off, paragraph structure and register adjustment with no new factual content; Note adds list and heading structure; Meeting notes permits summarization because that is its purpose and is bounded by a citation requirement in place of a recall threshold. All four declare that they do not answer questions. What the design claims about that declaration is bounded by what its checks can establish (D-012): the language-independent set always runs, and where a validator pack exists the language-dependent set checks that interrogatives in the normalized transcript survive in order, that content-word recall clears the threshold, and that no sentence lacks content-word support in the input. An observed violation retries once with a stricter instruction and then delivers the normalized transcript while retaining the generated text marked contract_violation. These are necessary conditions, not proof of fidelity, which is why the adversarial corpus and the rubric scoring rule in verification decide whether a built-in ships at all. Where no pack exists the model still runs and its output is still retained; only the delivered text falls back, and only when the mode declares answersQuestions false and the transcript contains an interrogative. A mode that answered dictated questions would have to declare that in its contract, which makes it visibly distinct in the mode indicator.

Users author prompts and formatting rules, and each custom mode also fills in a structured transformation contract naming its allowed operations, whether it may answer questions, its content bound and the languages its validator supports; the editor cannot save a mode without one, because a free-form prompt gives the checker nothing to check against (D-012). Each mode selects its own local speech and language models by content identity instead of by name (D-022). Every save creates a content-addressed revision in an append-only chain, and every run pins the revision id into its manifest at start along with model installations, vocabulary revision, language and validator pack set (D-006). Work already in progress reads its snapshot and never live settings, so editing a mode or switching models during a recognition cannot change what the running job produces. Saved results keep pointing at the revision that produced them, and History names that revision and diffs it against the current one, so a later edit cannot silently change the meaning of an earlier result. Because every result also names the run and its inputs (D-029), a rewrite produced by an old revision stays attributable even after the audio is recognized again under a different model. Model choice is never restricted by check coverage: a mode may select any compatible installation in any language, and what varies is which checks ran and what the panel reports.

Rules match the foreground application's bundle identifier and, where readable, the website URL,evaluated at arming with first match winning over a user-ordered list (D-014). List position is the complete precedence rule, so the answer is readable off the list top to bottom; specificity now only proposes an insertion point in the editor and flags rules an earlier rule shadows, which removes the undefined priority field the last review found. When a predicate's input cannot be obtained, because browser automation is denied, the browser exposes no URL, or screen recording is off, rules needing that input do not match and evaluation continues; if nothing matches, the user's default mode applies. Permission loss is handled per capability, so losing browser automation narrows rule matching without disturbing capture or recognition (D-032). The chosen mode is latched into the run manifest, so it cannot change mid-sentence, and the effective mode plus whether it came from a rule or the fallback appears in the recording panel and the menu bar for every run, which is what keeps the current mode apparent (D-011). Which browsers expose a URL is enumerated in a dated matrix before URL rules ship instead of assumed, and an incomplete matrix degrades to bundle-identifier rules.

User terminology and names enter at four points with a fixed order relative to recognition and language processing (D-015). Before recognition, selected terms go into the decoder's prompt slot, bounded by the runtime's limit and chosen by mode relevance and recency; that shifts decoding probabilities and the interface says exactly that, with no claim that adding a name guarantees recognition, because the mechanism is a prompt and not a decoding constraint (D-020). After recognition, configurable replacements run deterministically over the recognition result with longest-match-first, boundary-aware, case-preserving, non-overlapping, single-pass semantics, using ICU word segmentation for the run's language and falling back to substring matching with a warning where segmentation is unavailable. Filler removal is a separate per-mode pass after replacement. After generation the replacement table is applied once more, and vocabulary survival is one of the language-independent checks, so it runs whether or not a validator pack exists for the run's language (D-012); a language model that normalizes an unusual proper noun back to a common word is caught, and the user's spelling wins. Recognition and normalized results are both retained, so the effect of each stage is inspectable.

Three optional sources are sampled at arming in parallel against a 200 ms deadline: focused-element text, selection and window title through accessibility; one frame of the focused window through ScreenCaptureKit with Vision text recognition when opted in; and the first text item on the pasteboard, each capped (D-016). Sampling once at arming bounds cost and makes a run reproducible; anything missing the deadline is omitted and recorded as omitted. Retention defaults to a digest, byte length and source kind instead of the text, and every transient copy has a stated release point: the screen frame dies when Vision returns and never reaches disk, accessibility and pasteboard text die when the prompt is assembled, service buffers are released per credit window, and no inference service writes prompts or context to disk. Retaining text is opt-in per mode, shown in History and deleted with the recording. Missing permissions leave a named operating state: no Screen Recording means no screen context and no system audio while everything else continues, and losing Accessibility removes focused-element context without ending an in-flight run (D-032). Context is supplied as data, not instructions, and the design uses a runtime measure rather than only an after-the-fact check: screen text and pasteboard text reach the prompt as a capped term list by default, which removes instruction-shaped sentences from the prompt entirely, with prose per-mode opt-in recorded on the result (D-012). On the prose path the context overlap check rejects any span of eight or more tokens present in the context and absent from the transcript, and a violation retries once and then delivers the normalized transcript. That check detects copying and cannot detect compliance expressed in new words, which is why the distillation carries the primary weight and the claim is stated as a necessary condition. Context never leaves the machine: it crosses only an XPC connection to a service the system denies network access (D-028).

Recognition language is set per mode to an explicit code or to detection using the runtime's language identification with its probability; below the threshold the run records undetermined, uses the mode's default and the panel says so (D-017). Translation into English is a separate declared operation that inserts a result naming the exact recognition or normalized result it translated, so the source transcript is preserved beside any derived text and stays identifiable even after the same audio is recognized again under a different model (D-029). Recognition and rewriting are evaluated by different methods and reported separately, word error rate for the first and a scored human rubric for the second, because a rewrite score cannot distinguish a mis-recognized word from a badly reworded sentence. Compatibility is declared per model installation and checked against the per-kind runtime descriptor at activation (D-022); the interface attributes language claims to the model publisher and marks them unmeasured until an evaluation row exists, so no coverage is promised on documentation alone. Pack coverage does not restrict which models may be used or which languages may be rewritten: without a pack the model runs, the generated result is produced and retained, and the language-independent checks still apply, with the result marked checks_partial and the check list attached (D-012). Only the delivered text changes, and only when the mode declares answersQuestions false and the transcript contains an interrogative, which is the one case where the missing check is the one protecting the requirement.

Microphone, system audio and imported audio and video all implement one AudioSource that emits native-format frames carrying stream id, clock domain, presentation time, sequence and a discontinuity flag, with conversion to the canonical 16 kHz mono recognition input as an explicit stage after the port (D-018). Consumers grant credit, so a seekable source stops decoding when the recognizer falls behind and a live source that overruns records a discontinuity instead of buffering without bound; credit extends across the service connection, which is what bounds memory in both processes instead of in the decoder alone. The initial format matrix is what the system decoders cover: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v and mov. The extension mechanism is a DecoderProvider port with an opt-in external command-line decoder, off by default, run as a child of the sandboxed decode service; whether it inherits the restriction is tested directly at F2, and if it does not, the decoder stays off by default with the trust transfer stated (D-028). Files decode in 30-second windows, and the memory claim is tested as a slope across 10-minute, 1-hour and 3-hour imports measured in both the app and the speech service, since a single run in one process cannot establish independence from duration. A failed import leaves its source unchanged because the path opens it read-only, copies into the session directory, and commits only after the artifact is complete; on failure the directory is removed and no row exists (D-019). Imports run in the batch lane and yield to interactive dictation under the scheduler's policy, which is whole-job restart unless a descriptor records verified checkpoint equivalence, while the capture writer and sealer sit outside admission so an import cannot starve live capture (D-004).

A meeting captures microphone and system audio as two artifacts whose frames carry host-time stamps, so alignment and gaps are represented by the ingest port instead of reconstructed afterwards (D-018), and capture is crash-safe through the chunk journal with its stated commit order, so an interrupted meeting yields a sealed artifact per stream with a bounded tail loss (D-030). Channel origin is recorded as a fact about capture and labeled as the microphone channel and the system audio channel; it is not presented as speaker identity, because a microphone can pick up remote audio from speakers and a system stream can carry several applications (D-023). Speaker separation has an explicit runtime and an explicit home: SpeakerKit's Pyannote pipeline behind a Diarizer port, running in its own sandboxed DiarizationService with download disabled, an explicit model folder and explicit segmenter and embedder concurrency recorded in the manifest, with weights acquired by the user and never bundled. Diarization and note generation are stages of the run machine (D-006), so each has a cancellation effect, a recovery transition and admission accounting; the diarization model set counts against the residency budget alongside speech and generation rather than sitting outside it (D-027). Evidence is represented at the boundary the cited API declaration supports: per-segment calibrated confidence is unknown and no per-segment margin is stored, while centroid cosine distance, where a centroid exists, proposes cross-recording identity for user confirmation and never applies one. Segments default to unverified, and notes attribute only segments a user assigned or the model assigned with evidence. Editing speaker names appends an assignment revision and an identity-name entry, and a notes run pins the transcript, the diarization result, the assignment revision and the name-set hash in its manifest and in result_inputs, so a later rename or re-diarization cannot change what a saved note meant; History reports the drift and offers regeneration (D-037, D-029). Timestamped notes are generated locally over the transcript in overlapping windows with per-bullet segment citations and uncited bullets dropped. F5 inventories the fields the pinned SDK version actually exposes before the schema is frozen, and the evaluation methods for attribution quality are named in verification and remain unperformed, so no attribution accuracy is claimed.

Recordings are searchable through FTS5 over result text with bm25 ranking and snippets, and playable from the sealed artifact (D-005, D-024). Each recording expands into its processing runs, and each run into a result chain rooted at that run's recognition or diarization result, so reprocessing through another model or mode inserts a new run and new results while every earlier result stays immutable and attributable (D-029). The relationship between original audio and successive results is one recording to many runs to many results, with each result naming its primary input and, where it has several, its additional inputs by role, plus the mode revision and model installations that produced it. That is what lets History compare two recognitions or two diarizations of the same audio without ambiguity, and what keeps a note tied to the diarization and assignment revision it used. A user-movable pointer selects the displayed run. Deletion while processing is active sets a tombstone, increments a generation counter and signals cancellation; every worker carries the recording id and generation from admission and commits in one transaction that aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording because the check and the insert cannot be separated. Deletion requested before the sealing commit is recorded as a manifest disposition, since no row exists to tombstone yet (D-033). Retention is not a separate mechanism: age, size and audio-discarding policies acquire the same leases, skip recordings held by a worker or a player, and move audio to a discarded state that disables playback, re-recognition and re-diarization while leaving text reprocessing available. Interrupted work resolves through the state-indexed recovery contract, which covers diarizing and noting as well as the dictation stages, so a crash leaves committed results intact and offers a new run (D-031). Space is reported as deleting until the last lease releases.

The model library browses and manages installed speech, language and diarization models with their declared capabilities, sizes, per-asset licenses and owning runtime (D-022). Identity is publisher name, revision string and a SHA-256 over the ordered weight file set, so two quantizations under one name are distinguishable and a result names exactly what produced it. Compatibility is checked before activation against a per-kind descriptor, and the smoke test is per kind too, so a diarizer missing its clusterer or a speech model missing its tokenizer fails at install rather than mid-run. That test is a capability check and never a quality judgment: a compatible model with no benchmark row activates normally and is labeled unmeasured, and the evaluation harness and its acceptance ranges are development tooling for choosing shipped defaults that gate nothing in the application (D-034). Installation stages, verifies, smoke-tests, then renames into an immutable content-addressed blob directory that is never written again, after which one transaction records the installation with its notices and moves the active pointer; a crash between those steps leaves an unreferenced blob that garbage collection removes, and a run pinned to the previous installation holds a lease so its weights survive activation. A failed download or import therefore cannot replace a working installation, and a failed user import stays in staging with its error attached. Model loading never triggers a download: runtimes receive absolute paths, initializers that can fetch are prohibited by a build check, acquisition is confined to an explicitly invoked downloader on a host allowlist, and all four inference services are denied the network by their sandbox, with the fallback claim wording written in advance so a failed access method cannot silently weaken the contract (D-028, D-003, D-023). Replacing a runtime has bounded effect on storage and on the interface: runtimes are separate adapter targets and separate service binaries with their own descriptors and parameter schemas (D-002, D-020, D-021), common parameters render generically while runtime-specific ones may supply presentation hooks and old rows stay readable from params_rendered after an adapter is removed, and archiving releases weight blobs while retaining identity, hashes and notices, so History stays attributable without holding every superseded multi-gigabyte model (D-038). Activation of a pairing exceeding the residency budget, which now counts speech, generation and diarization together, is refused with the arithmetic shown, labeled measured or declared, and overridable by the user (D-027).

A menu bar status item is the always-available surface showing state, effective mode, recent results and settings, complementing the recording panel (D-011, D-025). Microphone level adjustment is software gain on captured buffers by default, with metering and a clipping indicator, so the common case changes no system state and has nothing to restore; setting the input device's hardware volume is opt-in and restored only if the current value still equals what the app set, with any mismatch leaving the setting as found and saying so. For media, the app restores playback only where it can own the change: a player adapter identifies the player, issues the pause to it, observes the transition to paused, and records that specific pause, and only such a pause is resumed automatically, and only while the player still reports paused. Where no adapter covers the playing application, the app may still post a play-pause key when the default output device reports a running client, records the pause as unattributed, and offers Resume playback as an explicit user action for ten minutes; no setting turns that into automatic resumption, because a media-key toggle and an idle output device establish neither the recipient nor the transition, and the specification states that opting in does not remove that condition. Competing applications and manual user edits therefore produce no automatic restoration and a note that playback or the setting was left as found. Losing automation permission for a player removes its adapter and drops that player to the unattributed path (D-032). The macOS baseline and the public APIs these behaviors use are set by D-001, with anything newer behind an availability check and a defined fallback.

open_questions.question: Can a sandboxed XPC service with the network client entitlement withheld load the chosen model weights for each model kind, including a runtime that opens a model directory by path, and does the external decoder it spawns inherit the restriction?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F2, before the entitlement set and the model-access path are frozen. Load each model kind by both candidate mechanisms, descriptor passing and a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs; attempt outbound connections and a write outside the job scratch directory and assert both fail; repeat from the spawned decoder. Not blocking because both the mechanism and the fallback are already decided: if the sandbox blocks loading by both mechanisms for a runtime, that runtime moves to an unsandboxed service and D-028 already contains the exact narrowed claim text for it, which still satisfies the requirement that captured audio, transcripts and context stay on the Mac. The change is visible in the product's stated guarantee rather than silent.

open_questions.question: How does the shipping speech runtime behave on long input and under cancellation: peak resident size as a function of duration, cancellation latency, whether a resumed checkpoint reproduces the unpreempted transcript, and does it meet the accuracy and latency ranges for the default pairing?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F1, with ranges and failure actions approved under D-035 before it runs: no more than 15 percent relative worse word error rate than the fallback adapter on the same audio, p50 at most 3.0 s and p95 at most 6.0 s to final transcript for a 30-second utterance, and a 3-hour peak within 500 MB of the 10-minute peak. Actions on failure are recorded with each range. The runtime choice itself is made in D-020 on integration, licensing and dependency evidence; these measurements evaluate it, and the whisper.cpp adapter behind the same port satisfies the same requirement if a range is missed.

open_questions.question: How much captured audio is lost when the writer is killed at an arbitrary offset, and can the packet table always be reconstructed from the durable index prefix?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F3, before recovery expectations for the capturing and sealing states are approved. Kill the writer at randomized offsets across chunk boundaries and both fsync points, recover, and assert a maximum lost interval of at most 4 seconds over at least 200 trials with every artifact decoding end to end. If the interval is exceeded, shorten the chunk period and re-measure. If reconstruction is ever invalid, adopt the structural fallback in D-030 and retain journal chunks until the finalized artifact has been decoded and hashed, which costs journal storage rather than correctness.

open_questions.question: Which insertion paths preserve existing field content and allow the confirmation predicate to be evaluated in the target applications, and when does each target read the pasteboard?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F4, before per-application delivery profiles ship. Prototype rung 1 and rung 2 with readback in the applications listed under verification, recording whether existing content survives, whether the predicate is evaluable, and pasteboard read timing and snapshot cost by content type. The ladder does not wait on the table, because its default for an unmeasured target is one attempt whose non-evaluable outcome is unconfirmed, with the transcript left on the pasteboard and Copy and Deliver offered. The table removes avoidable holds and sets the snapshot limit from data rather than from the current starting value.

open_questions.question: Which fields does the pinned SpeakerKit version actually expose in DiarizationResult, which speakers receive centroids on multi-speaker fixtures, what do the segmenter and embedder cost in resident size and wall time, and do the download flag and model folder suppress acquisition under a network-denied profile?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F5, a thin adapter experiment before the meeting schema and the diarization residency numbers are frozen. RESEARCH establishes centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers and establishes that per-segment confidence and margin are not exposed, so the schema already stores unknown for those; F5 confirms the field list at the pinned version and supplies the numbers admission needs. Not blocking because the structural fallback is recorded: if centroids are unavailable for a speaker, cross-recording naming for that speaker becomes a user action with no automatic proposal, and if segment identifiers prove unstable across runs, assignment carry-forward switches to time-range overlap (D-037).

open_questions.question: Which languages get validator packs at ship, and how often does a missing pack change the delivered text for users who wanted the rewrite?
open_questions.resolution: Ship the English pack with the first generation modes and add packs driven by the measured checks_partial and fallback rates per language. No model or language is blocked in the meantime, and the per-mode setting that delivers generated text under partial checks records itself on the result, so the cost of a missing pack is measurable rather than assumed.

open_questions.question: Which browsers expose the current URL through accessibility, and which need automation permission or provide nothing?
open_questions.resolution: Enumerate per browser and record a dated table before URL rules ship. The rule engine treats an unreadable URL as a non-match, so an incomplete table degrades to bundle-identifier rules and the default mode.

open_questions.question: Is FTS5 compiled into the system SQLite on the chosen baseline?
open_questions.resolution: A runtime check during store setup. If absent, build GRDB against a bundled SQLite, accepting a larger binary and an update obligation, and record the change against D-005.

open_questions.question: Is an 8B-class instruct model at 4-bit quantization the right default for Email and Meeting notes on the 16 GB target, given that diarization now shares the budget?
open_questions.resolution: Score two or three sizes against the fidelity corpus under the rubric rule, recording violation and checks_partial rates per model, and pair the result with the F5 diarization footprint so the recommended default fits the budget with meetings running. Model selection is per mode either way, so a wrong default is a settings change.

open_questions.question: Can the provisional live pass run alongside capture without dropping frames or degrading the final pass on the target machine, and if not, which rung of the preview ladder does?
open_questions.resolution: Measure alongside F1: capture with and without the full provisional pass, then with a smaller preview model, then with batched updates at voice-activity pauses, comparing dropped frame counts, final word error rate and time to final transcript. The lowest acceptable rung ships. If no rung meets the bars, that is a release question for the product owner under D-035, not a removal of the requirement (D-011).

open_questions.question: Which diarization weight assets may be offered for download rather than only imported?
open_questions.resolution: Compile the notice inventory per asset against the component-specific references RESEARCH records for the embedder and clusterer. The feature ships either way, because weights are user-acquired through the model store and an asset whose notice does not permit redistribution stays importable; the inventory decides only what the downloader offers.
